report.summary: An incident occurred where about 30% of portfolio screen loads failed starting at 13:43 on 2026-10-09. The root cause was identified as memory exhaustion in portfolio-service due to the deployment of version v3.8.0 (chg-7001), which introduced in-memory per-user holdings snapshots. This caused memory usage to steadily climb starting at 12:53, reach full saturation at 13:44, and trigger container OOM kills and pod restarts starting at 13:42. Consequently, portfolio-service and mobile-bff experienced connection resets and error rate spikes starting at 13:43.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Portfolio-service Memory Exhaustion via v3.8.0 Snapshot Feature

supporting.note: Deployed portfolio-service v3.8.0 which explicitly stores per-user holdings snapshots in memory.
Shows memory usage starting an upward climb at 12:53 and reaching saturation (106.64%) just before the incident.
Pod restarts began at 13:42, right before the error spike.
Error rate spiked sharply starting at 13:43.
mobile-bff logged upstream connection reset errors calling portfolio-service starting at 13:43.

contradicting.note: p99 latency remained flat without significant anomaly during the window, though failing/restarting pods drop requests rather than hanging.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Portfolio-db v1.1.0 Release Causes Blocking and Memory Pressure

supporting.note: portfolio-db was deployed with v1.1.0 shortly before the incident onset.
portfolio-service memory saturation occurred after the database deploy.
portfolio-service error rate rose sharply after the database update.

contradicting.note: p99 latency did not show an increase as would typically be expected from database blocking or slow queries.
CPU utilization remained completely normal and flat, inconsistent with heavy database serialization or query parsing overhead.

facts.text: portfolio-service was deployed with v3.8.0 keeping per-user holdings snapshots in memory on 2026-10-08T18:20:00+00:00.
portfolio-db was deployed with v1.1.0 on 2026-10-09T12:27:00+00:00.
portfolio-service memory percentage showed an anomaly starting upward from 12:53, reaching a peak of 106.64% at 13:44 and becoming saturated.
portfolio-service pod restarts began upward from 13:42, reaching a peak of 2.09 restarts/min at 13:46.
portfolio-service error rate spiked starting at 2026-10-09T13:43:00+00:00, reaching a peak of 32.73%.
mobile-bff error rate increased starting at 2026-10-09T13:43:00+00:00, reaching a peak of 10.23%.
mobile-bff logged upstream portfolio-service connection reset errors starting at 2026-10-09T13:43:00+00:00.

assumptions: The in-memory holdings snapshots accumulate without proper eviction or are large enough under normal production loads to exceed container memory limits.

timeline.event: portfolio-service v3.8.0 deployed keeping per-user holdings snapshots in memory.
portfolio-service memory percentage begins upward climb from baseline 75.09%.
portfolio-service and mobile-bff error rates spike; mobile-bff logs upstream connection resets to portfolio-service.

recommended_actions.action: Roll back portfolio-service to version v3.7.2 to remove the in-memory per-user holdings snapshot feature.
recommended_actions.rationale: Version v3.8.0 introduced the snapshot storage that directly leads to memory saturation and container OOM kills.

recommended_actions.action: Implement a memory limit increase or proper eviction policy for user holdings snapshots if the v3.8.0 feature is to be re-introduced.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents future memory exhaustion and container restarts caused by unmanaged in-memory data growth.
